notes: Genuine one-time inspection of the exact render at masterSha256 597ba2ad...78fb1e, produced by offlineGeneratedPlanRender.ts rendering the ACTUAL generated six-beat production plan for compare-rtx4080s-rtx4080 (issue #89) — not offlineCompositorSmoke.ts's earlier hand-authored 3-visual/8-second timeline. The onScreenText caption (the idea's full title, 78 characters) is the first exercise of a caption this long anywhere in this pipeline — see the next note.

CAPTION-WRAP DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS REVIEW: captionRender.ts's wrapCaption() previously collapsed any caption needing MORE than two wrapped lines into one unwrapped second line (joined with spaces, no width limit), which rendered wider than the 1080px safe area — confirmed by direct inspection: the beat-1 caption ran off both the left and right edges of the frame in the render produced before this fix. Root-caused to wrapCaption's line-count fallback and fixed there (now truncates the overflow remainder to maxChars with an ellipsis instead of leaving it unwrapped); regression test added (mediaRender.test.ts, 'caption wrapping'). The masterSha256 and frames recorded in this file are from the render produced AFTER that fix, not before — the caption in beat1-hook-t0.2s.png reads 'Pick the GPU before / SpecSmith reveals the names…', fully inside the frame.

Avg FPS: 160' both correctly labeled Estimated, 'Better Value' badge, 20-0 tally, per-game bar chart. Caption 'LOCK YOUR PICK' fully inside frame. No consent banner.

REAL LIMITATION, not scored around: beats 2 through 6 (5 of the video's 6 beats) show the IDENTICAL captured Compare-page state — productionPlan.ts's deriveUiRenderState derives one static (not sequence) UI state per plan and every non-hook beat reuses it (see productionPlan.ts's buildTasks comment: 'every UI beat in a plan depicts the same verified state'). The video is visually repetitive across those 5 beats; only the burned-in caption text and narration change. This is a real, pre-existing characteristic of the generated plan this render wires through — not something offlineGeneratedPlanRender.ts introduced or something this PR's scope covers fixing (it would mean changing how productionPlan.ts derives UI beat state, a broader design decision). Reflected honestly in visualCoherenceScore/pacingScore below rather than inflated.

No fake/generated UI anywhere presented as real: the one non-UI beat (the hook) is a plain, clearly labeled offline fixture card, never claiming to be SpecSmith UI or paid-generated video (see uiShots below). No fabricated benchmark/price data — every number in the real-UI beats is the app's own estimateFpsForBuild()/gpus.json/cpus.json output.

Audio: this review did NOT include literal audio playback (no listening capability in this environment). What was verified: ffmpeg silencedetect (noise=-35dB, d=0.3s) over the full 25.338s master reports zero silence intervals — narration is continuous with no dropouts; ffmpeg volumedetect reports mean -21.7dB / max -2.0dB, a healthy non-clipping level, not silence and not distortion. Narration runs at 220wpm (localFixtureTts.ts's default 165wpm was too slow to fit the full six-beat script — see offlineGeneratedPlanRender.ts's comment on this) via espeak-ng, the same deterministic formant synthesizer the original offline evidence already used; its output stays word-distinguishable through roughly this rate, faster and more rushed-sounding than the original 165wpm smoke narration but not degraded to noise. audioClarityScore below reflects that basis (verified continuity/levels plus known engine behavior at this rate), not a subjective listen.

Confirmed across two separate renders of this exact committed code during this review that the rendered bytes are NOT reproducible run to run even though the on-screen content is identical (same root cause as offlineCompositorSmoke.ts's prior finding: ffmpeg's own encode/mux is not guaranteed byte-identical, plus MP4 container metadata) — this evidence file is bound to the one specific masterSha256 above, not to 'renders that look like this'.
